extracted.intended_audience: editors, proofreaders, typesetters, and authors preparing manuscripts for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for copyediting, punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation, typography, and typesetting conventions for preparing manuscripts and printed works, as used by a university press style manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for division of words, systems of division, use of hyphen to indicate divisions, avoidance of unnecessary divisions, and special rules for two-letter divisions and foreign words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rules referenced (182; 210; 215; 221; 231). Avoid dividing on certain letters and avoid unnecessary or awkward divisions (e.g., two-letter syllables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivatives capitalization and formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on derivatives from Greek and Latin, from proper names, and English derivatives from scientific names (not capitalized); treatment affects hyphenation and division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes differentiation rules and examples (pages cited 115, 53, 46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional mark placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not place divisional mark at end of middle of sentences; avoid placing a divisional mark at the end of the line within sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rule 220 for divisional mark usage; avoid breaking readability by splitting sentences awkwardly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of titles of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize principal words in titles of publications; guidance on when titles should be italicized or roman-quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See multiple entries: capitalization (41), italicizing (60), roman-quoted (80-83); definite article not part of newspaper title (43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of political divisions and organizational names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for political divisions, numbered divisions to be spelled out, and capitalization of names of governmental departments, legislative bodies, judiciary bodies, institutions, and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: political divisions (6-7), governmental departments (13), legislative bodies (18), judiciary bodies (12), organizations (11). Spell out numbered divisions (100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of University divisions and official units
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of divisions, departments, officers, courses, and units of study in official work dealing with the University of Chicago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidance for the University of Chicago (49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of double dagger for footnote index
rubrics_metrics.description: Use double dagger symbol for one of the footnote indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rule 23a; multiple symbols (¶, §, etc.) addressed elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of double rules in tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use double rules (double lines) in tables where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See tables and rules sections (243, 247, 347) for how rules are used in tabular work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogation point for doubt or query
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interrogation point (question mark) to express doubt or query in certain contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See entry 'Doubt' (229) and 'Query' (129). Guidance on punctuation placement with quotations is given elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of Dutch and foreign particles (Van, Von, Mc, Mac, M')
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalizing and indexing Dutch names and treatment of prefixes/particles in proper nouns (Van, Von, Mc, Mac, M').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See indexing rules (240) and specific treatment (3; 340).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization and spelling of dynasties and historical epochs
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of names of dynasties (Egyptian) and historical/geological epochs; to be spelled out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dynasties (13; 100); epochs (14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' and proofreaders' hints and marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Hints for editors and proofreaders, including marks of proofreaders and instructions for proof corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See editors' hints (pp. 1x3-16) and proofreaders' marks (p. 123); descriptive sections on proofs (285-89) and proof stages (foundry, plate, page-proof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of roman (upright) vs. italic type for abbreviations (e.g., E.g., I.e.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set certain abbreviations (E.g., I.e.) in roman type rather than italic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. to be set in roman (62); I.e. in roman (61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suffixes to titles (elect, ex-, 'vice')
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of suffixes like 'elect', prefix 'ex-', and titles prefixed by 'vice' and how they affect capitalization and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: 'Elect' (201), 'Ex-' (20X), 'vice' prefixed to titles (30x). See corresponding rules for capitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of ellipses, treatment as part of a quotation, and use to indicate omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rules 180-81; treat ellipses as part of quotation (88, 188); use to indicate omissions (180).

rubrics_metrics.name: Em-dash and en-dash definitions and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and illustrations of em-dash and en-dash and their specific uses (e.g., em-dash for 'to' in time, en-dash in ranges and as substitute for hyphen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Em-dash defined and illustrated (261; 173); en-dash defined and illustrated (261; 158, 183, 173). See dash usage for emphasis, pause, transition, and summarizing clauses (166-170, 270).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis (use of dashes, exclamation points, italics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for indicating emphasis in text: use of dashes, exclamation points, and italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: emphasis by dashes (168), exclamation points (127), italics (58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling English equivalents of foreign words/phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: When a foreign word or phrase is given, the English equivalent should be quoted; foreign words in English text often set in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English equivalent to be quoted (78); foreign words in italics (59); translations/roman-quoting rules (78, 82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerations and parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of parentheses in enumerations connected with letters or figures indicating subdivisions; punctuation of enumerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rule 176 and related guidance on sub-section numbering and sequences (176, 153).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of epithets and proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: When epithets are used as proper names they are capitalized; rules for proper nouns and possessives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epithets capitalized when proper names (2); proper names capitalization and possessive formation guidance (1, 113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of events, movements, peoples, tribes, and places
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize important historical events, movements, peoples, races, tribes, and place-names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events (15), movements (16), peoples/tribes/races (47), place-names foreign treatment (59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and use of exclamation point
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of the exclamation point and special uses such as exclamatory 'Oh' and ironic usages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclamation point rules (127-28); exclamatory 'Oh' (117); ironic word/phrase uses of quotation marks and exclamation (77, 127).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation/clarification brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use brackets for interpolations and explanations of technical terms and to indicate inserted explanations or omissions within quoted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of brackets for explanations (178); interpolations (178); technical term explanations (258-94).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics: definition and rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of italics and comprehensive rules for when to use italics: titles, names of genera and species, emphasis, foreign words, astronomical names, legal cases, and other specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See detailed list: italics defined (254) and rules 54-73 (titles of works, foreign words, emphasis, letters, symbols, names of genera/species, etc.). Exceptions noted for long bibliographies (need not use italics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small caps and caps-and-small-caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and guidance for use of small caps and cap-and-small-caps (e.g., section headings, 'Section' and 'Whereas' in resolutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small caps defined and uses (357; 51); 'Section' and 'Whereas' uses (51, 72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign languages in quotations and typography
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle sentences and passages quoted from foreign languages, including when to reduce quotations, whether to use quotation marks, and italicization of foreign words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on quoted foreign-language passages (59, 85); treat English translation as quoted (78); italics for foreign words (59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ligatures and digraphs in typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on ligature usage (æ, ſ, etc.) in Latin and other languages; digraphs treated as single letters for division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latin non-use of certain ligatures (115); digraphs/ligature treatment referenced under 'Digraphs' and 'Ligature'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and numerals: usage, spacing, and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using figures (numerals) in text: when to spell out numbers, grouping and punctuation rules, spacing of Arabic and Roman numerals at beginning of lines and headlines, and omission of periods after numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See numbers rules (94-98, 159, 173, 271-278). Spell out numbers that commence a sentence (96); set groups of six or more figures in figures; treatment of round numbers (95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of names of newspapers, periodicals, and serial titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize principal words in periodical titles; italicize names of newspapers and periodicals; do not treat the article 'The' as part of the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicals: capitalization (41); italicize (60); definite article not treated as part of title (43); serial titles roman-quoted (80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes: numbering, indices, placement, and style
rubrics_metrics.description: General style for footnotes, numbering sequences, placing of the index figure, indices for references to footnotes, exceptions to general style, and samples of footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 232-39 cover numbering, placement (236), sequences (232), and special cases; Linotype/Monotype specific rules for footnotes (239).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing rules and cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for indexing proper names, treatment of prefixes and particles, italics for 'See'/'See also' in cross-references, and placing of index entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing guidance (240); italicizing 'See' and 'See also' (62); indexing of Umlaut and 'St.' names (240, 340).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenization and hyphenated words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for hyphenization, lists of hyphenated words, avoidance of dividing hyphenated words across lines, and number of consecutive hyphens allowed at line ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenization rules (182-234); hyphenated words list (214); avoid dividing hyphenated words (225); max consecutive hyphens at line ends (247?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of apostrophes for omitted letters and omission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use apostrophes to indicate omitted figures or letters in the middle of words; rules for omission of letters and punctuation such as periods after headlines and Roman numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of figures or letters indicated by apostrophe (163); omission of period after headlines (135) and Roman numerals (124); dates omission rules (202).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation: general rules and special contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for punctuation: placement of commas, periods, semicolons, colons, question/exclamation marks with quotations, punctuation of extracts and classical references, and punctuation with indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules sections 122-140, 220-224, 237-239. Placement of punctuation with quotation marks addressed (126, 136, 140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks and treatment of quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of quotation marks, when to omit them (reduced citations or certain headings), double vs. single quotes, placement of punctuation with quotes, and special rules for extracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 74-91; exceptions for reduced citations (87); punctuation placement with quotation marks (126, 136, 163, 281).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of shorter works vs. longer works (roman-quoted vs italic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when to set titles of shorter works (poems, articles) in roman-quote vs when to italicize titles of books and longer works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short poems, articles roman-quoted (81-83); books and major works italicized (60); specific categories listed (essays, lectures, pamphlets, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings, headlines, and running heads
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format headings and headlines, omit period after headlines, spacing of headlines, and rules for running heads including omission of period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headings described (379-83); headlines spacing (371); omission of period after headlines and runnings-heads (135, 383).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work: open and ruled tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting tables: open tables (two-column) vs ruled tables (more than two columns), how to set headlines and box-heads, specimen tables and reading-matter treatment, spacing of columns for figures/percentages/totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabular rules 241-50; specimen tables (350); reading-matter spacing (345-346); use of different type for totals and percentages (241).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing: importance and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for spacing in composition: standard spacing, different sizes of spaces, spacing in foundry/linotype/monotype composition, spacing of divisional signs, figure columns, headlines, short words, and what is considered good spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive coverage (358-373); standard spacing samples (363); avoid hair-spacing and excessive wide spacing (265, 365).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical terms, units, and type sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and explanations of typographical units, faces, quads, ems, point sizes, pica, nonpareil, minion, and sizes/styles of type in ordinary use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology explained (251-261, 352-357); specimen type pages provided; typographical unit on monotype (359).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of scientific names and technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of italics and capitalization for scientific names (genera and species), paleontological, geological, zoological, and medical terms; avoidance of italics for medical terms in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italics for genera/species (71); use of capitals in scientific terms (46); medical terms italics to be avoided (71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and symbols: handling and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of abbreviations (vol., chap., p.), metric and monetary symbols, percent expressions, and spacing rules for units and symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviation rules (123, 237); metric symbols spacing (269); per cent expressed in figures (94); use of 'p.' for page (237).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of superior figures and indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of superior figures (superscripts) for reference indices and footnote sequences and guidance on placing index figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superior figures for reference indices (333, 334); placing of index figure (236); sequences of footnote indices (232, 333).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraphs and indention styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of paragraph types (plain, regular), styles of paragraphs, first-line indention rules, and hanging indention definition and settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs explained (284); indention rules 274-76; hanging indention defined and illustrated (279, 284, 376).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations from poetry and prose: capitalization and indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of first words in lines of poetry, indentation rules for poetry, when to reduce and run poetry/prose into text, and treatment of quoted passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems: first word capitalization in English lines (34); poetry indention (275); reductions rules (85-87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of punctuation with indices and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement of punctuation (periods, commas) in relation to indices in the text and punctuation in classical and Scripture references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement rules (126, 237-239); punctuation with indices (332-334); use of semicolons in Scripture references (139).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parentheses and brackets for nested punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using parentheses and when to use brackets within parentheses for nested interpolations or explanatory matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parentheses rules (176-78); within parentheses use brackets (178); placement of periods with parentheses (126).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of plurals and possessives
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for forming plurals (including of abbreviations and numerals) and possessives of proper names, especially those ending in sibilants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural formation (165); possessives guidance including names ending in sibilant (213); plurals of numerals and abbreviations (165, 210).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling conventions and variant spellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists and rules for spelling words with more than one accepted form, lists for ages, centuries, Christian names, names of publications, states, sessions of Congress, and decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spelling rules and lists (93-220); specific entries for many word families and conventions (e.g., 'Railroad'/'Railway' (204)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dates, time indications, and place-of-publication lines
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat dates (omit j, d, th), time of day expressions, punctuation of time indications, and formatting of place-of-publication and publisher lines (use of colon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates rules (202); time of day and punctuation (98, 134); place/publisher colon (135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of section, paragraph, and other legal/document symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing and use of section mark, paragraph mark, and other symbols used as footnote indices or to indicate sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section mark spacing and use (369, 333); paragraph mark used for footnote index (232).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of religious and legal terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for sacred books, New and Old Testament book abbreviations, pronouns referring to Deity, juridical acts, laws, bills, treaties, and titles of legal causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sacred books (39); pronouns for Deity (24); juridical acts capitalization (18); legal titles italicized (63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of addresses, salutations, and signatures in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting salutatory phrases, signatures, omission of commas and periods after signatures, and formatting of town/state in datelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salutatory phrase setting (50); signatures omission of comma (262) and period (235); town/state dateline formatting (50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special typographic ornaments and initial letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and examples of initials, ornaments, borders, and miscellaneous signs in typographic specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens and guidance in types section (95-116); initial letter usage and samples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of lists, series, and the serial comma
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of comma before final 'and', 'or', 'nor' in series; use of semicolons to separate clauses in enumerations; punctuation of series and sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series comma guidance (143); semicolon use in enumerations (138); punctuation to separate distinct clauses (137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of legal and formal documents (resolutions, proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to introduce paragraphs in resolutions, setting of 'Resolved' and 'Whereas' (cap-and-small-caps, italics), and formatting of proceedings titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolutions guidance (39, 51, 72); 'Resolved' set in italics (72); proceedings titles italicized (60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of abbreviations for biblical references and versions of the Bible
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of abbreviations for New and Old Testament books, versions, and punctuation/spacing of scripture passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations lists (109); Scripture punctuation (234, 239); spacing rules (372-373).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quotation techniques for unusual or emphasized words
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quotation marks for unusual words, terms to which attention is directed, or technical words used as words, and when quotation marks should be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks for unusual words (77, 79); omit for Preface, Index, etc. (83); single vs double quote rules (91).
